facts: The frozen fixture has exactly two implementation tasks and both require the same repository write surface.
At the canonical LoopX revision, adaptive admission treats the first admitted write lane as primary and blocks an overlapping later lane with write_scope_conflict.
When the frozen pair leaves no selected child lane, build_adaptive_task_orchestration_contract returns no adaptive task-orchestration contract.
The canonical Turn driver projects child host operations and subagent_execution_topology only from task_orchestration_contract_v2 adaptive eligible_child_lanes.
Executing the two tasks serially in one parent agent would not satisfy the preregistered requirement for distinct S1 workers.
The preregistered control removes LoopX adaptive S2 while retaining the same two-worker operational surface.
Without a native LoopX child topology, the canonical built-in Codex Turn has no first-party typed child-operation or child-receipt surface for this frozen pair.
Replacing that missing surface with a benchmark-authored subprocess launcher or merge coordinator would violate the preregistered control boundary.

forbidden_repairs: add a third non-overlapping task to make an adaptive bundle materialize
change or misdeclare the frozen task write scopes
replace the frozen tasks after observing the feasibility failure
count two sequential turns by the same parent agent as distinct S1 workers
use a benchmark-authored child launcher or adaptive merge coordinator as LoopX S2

evidence.claim: overlapping write scopes are blocked; no selected child means no adaptive contract
child host operations are projected only for adaptive v2 eligible child lanes
write-scope overlap is serialized and conflicting lanes are typed write_scope_conflict
without subagent_execution_topology the built-in Codex prompt omits LoopX child execution instructions and the result schema omits child receipts
adaptive child admission requires mutually non-overlapping write scopes; admission is permission rather than a command to spawn

reopen_conditions: A new-ref LoopX reassessment establishes a first-party observable model-owned path that can arbitrate the exact frozen two-task overlapping-write case while still executing two distinct S1 workers.
A separate newly preregistered experiment freezes a different fixture/control before any execution; it must not retroactively alter this preregistration.
